test.title: A café or restaurant you enjoy going to

document.cue: Describe a café or restaurant you enjoy going to.

text: The place I'd like to talk about is a small café called Tandyr, which is in a quiet side street not far from my university in Almaty. I first went there with classmates in my first year, and now I go at least once a week, usually on Fridays after lectures.

It's not fancy at all. There are only about eight tables, the walls are covered with old black-and-white photos of the city, and the owner, a cheerful woman in her fifties, is usually behind the counter herself. She remembers regular customers' names, which makes you feel welcome straight away.

I almost always order the same thing: samsa straight from the clay oven and a pot of black tea with milk. The samsa is so hot that you have to wait a couple of minutes before you can bite into it. If I'm really hungry, I add a bowl of lagman, which is enormous and costs less than a sandwich in a chain coffee shop.

I enjoy going there because it feels like the opposite of the big shopping-centre cafés. Nobody is in a hurry, there's no loud music, and you can sit for two hours with a book without anyone asking you to leave. It's become my favourite place to think or to have a proper conversation.
I just hope it never becomes too popular, or I might not get a table.

tips.en: So hot that you have to wait … lets the listener almost taste it.

note.en: “Makes you feel people are glad you came”.
Where and how often — the name, the location and the Friday routine.

note.ru: Где и как часто — название, место и привычка ходить по пятницам.

note.en: What it looks like — a small café and an owner who remembers customers.
note.kk: Қандай көрінеді — шағын кафе және қонақтарды есте сақтайтын иесі.
note.ru: Как выглядит — маленькое кафе и хозяйка, которая помнит гостей.

note.en: What the speaker orders — samsa from the clay oven, tea and lagman.
